_about: What a phone's home network and uptime look like, as data. The LAN address is reported BY the app (metasec report /#7/#5 iip, built from SIOCGIFCONF + RTM_GETROUTE), not connected from, so a proxy cannot change it and a shared one ties the cohort together regardless of exit IP. lan_section.py applies this file and holds no numbers of its own.
_source: The recorded phone was 192.168.1.17 behind 192.168.1.1 with 68893 s of uptime - one moment of one phone. The subnet shares below are how consumer routers hand out private ranges, stated as data rather than claimed as measurements.

subnets._: the ranges a router's own default puts a home network on, 192.168.1.x most often
the rest of the common 192.168.x space
routers that default to the 10/8 range

_host_in_dhcp_pool: a router hands addresses out of a pool: .100-.199 on most, .2-.99 on the rest. Never .1, which is the router itself.
_gateway_host: the router's own address inside the subnet: .1 on nearly every consumer router

uptime_bands._: up for a day or three
most phones are not rebooted for weeks

_uptime_bands: how long the phone has been up. badger's boot time (fts 12) is derived as now - uptime, so this governs that too and the two stay consistent.
